name: らー麺創房 ぱこ (Ramen Soubou Pako)

claims.text: Wheat ramen noodles are central to every bowl and are boiled in shared water; the broths and shio/shoyu tare are not gluten-free.
Soy-based (shoyu/chuka soba) bowls are on the menu; standard Japanese soy sauce contains wheat and no wheat-free tare is indicated.
Broths are built on dried sardine, mackerel, and bonito (fish), and pork-based noodles and gyoza are served; no plant-based preparation is offered.
The broth is a soy-sauce (shoyu) tare base; standard Japanese shoyu contains wheat, and the shop publishes no gluten-free or wheat-free tare.
All bowls use animal broth (pork bone / chicken) and pork chashu; no separate vegetable stock or vegan prep is mentioned.

name: ラーメン たぬき屋 (Ramen Tanukiya)

claims.text: Wheat noodles for ramen and mazesoba come from a Kyoto noodle maker and are boiled in the same shared pots; with a single nine-seat counter kitchen, gluten cross-contact is unavoidable.
Bowls use standard Japanese shoyu/tare seasoning, which is wheat-based; no wheat-free or tamari alternative is indicated.
All broths and bowls are pork- and chicken-based with chashu and meat toppings; no plant-based preparation exists, so any item will contain or contact animal products.

name: ラーメン 天 本店 (Ramen Ten Honten)

claims.text: Wheat ramen noodles are boiled in shared water and the shop also fries chicken karaage, so gluten exposure is unavoidable.
The bowl is a soy (shoyu) tare ramen; standard Japanese shoyu contains wheat.
Broth is pork-bone based and ramen is topped with pork, so no dish is free of animal products.

name: ラーメン てんぐ 西陣店 (Ramen Tengu Nishijin)

claims.text: Wheat ramen noodles are boiled in shared water and the broth is a pork-bone/dashi base with a presumed wheat shoyu tare; no gluten-free handling is described.
The bowl is described as a shoyu-style (soy-sauce) ramen, which in a shop like this is virtually always a wheat-containing soy sauce; no wheat-free tare is indicated.
All bowls are based on animal broth (pork bone plus Japanese dashi) and topped with pork chashu; no vegan or vegetable broth is offered.

name: ラーメン ビスカ (Ramen Viska)

claims.text: Wheat ramen noodles are boiled in shared water, making the broth and any shared utensils unsuitable for strict gluten avoidance.
Tare/seasoning is standard ramen-shop shoyu, which is wheat-containing soy sauce; no wheat-free tare is offered.
All broths are pork-bone based and every bowl is cooked in the same tonkotsu kitchen with pork chashu; no vegan-safe preparation exists.

name: らーめんや亜喜英 (Ramen-ya Akihide)

claims.text: Wheat ramen noodles cooked in a shared pot; broth and tare are not gluten-free. No gluten-free handling described.
Tare is almost certainly wheat-based soy sauce, as is standard for this style; no gluten-free tare offered.
Broth is pork-bone and chicken-bone based with pork chashu; no vegan preparation, and animal stock is the core of every bowl.

name: ラーメン ゆう (Ramen Yu)

claims.text: Single small counter kitchen built entirely around wheat ramen noodles, wheat-based shoyu tare, and gyoza; no separation possible and no GF handling mentioned.
The defining flavor is a soy-sauce (shoyu) tare, which in a traditional Kyoto ramen shop is wheat-based; assume the broth/tare contains wheat.
Broth is pork-based with chashu pork; no plant-based broth or vegan options, so vegan cross-contact is unavoidable.
